description:
Most of what you think you know about geography is probably wrong. There aren’t necessarily seven continents. Sweden has more islands than Indonesia. Alaska is both the westernmost and easternmost U.S. state. The Great Wall of China can’t easily be seen from space. And the Mercator map makes entire countries look wildly larger than they really are.

Some myths come from outdated facts, others come from distorted maps, confusing borders, strange time zones, or the way our brains simplify the world around us.
From hidden continents and misplaced capitals to rivers that flow backward and countries spanning multiple hemispheres, these 50 geography facts prove that the world is far stranger than the maps we grew up with.

description:
The U.S. debt crisis just got uglier. America spent years borrowing at ultra-low interest rates. Now trillions of dollars in old debt must be refinanced at much higher rates, and the interest bill is exploding.

Annual interest costs have already climbed past $1 Trillion, consuming a growing share of federal revenue while competing with defense, infrastructure, healthcare, and other spending. At the same time, demand for long-term Treasury bonds is weakening. That means Washington has to offer higher yields to attract buyers, making future borrowing even more expensive. 

The U.S. isn’t about to suddenly default. The bigger danger is slower and harder to see. More tax revenue going toward interest, higher borrowing costs across the economy, and less money available for everything else.
